The Quad leaders have announced a series of initiatives to strengthen maritime security, artificial intelligence cooperation, cybersecurity and critical infrastructure connectivity across the Indo-Pacific at Manila Summit in Philippines. The summit brought together Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. In a joint press release, the four leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open, safe and prosperous Indo-Pacific, describing the Quad as a “partnership of action” dedicated to peace, stability and prosperity. The four countries also announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, scheduled to be held in early 2027.

<><><> 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi returned to New Delhi after successfully concluding his two-day visit to Manila, the Philippines. During the visit, Mr Modi participated in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, the 21st East Asia Summit and the Quad Leaders’ Meeting. The Prime Minister also visited the historic Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila and took part in the ceremony marking the commencement of its redevelopment.

At the Quad Summit, Mr Modi said for India, the Quad is a “constructive and trusted” partnership that strives to deliver trusted solutions across the Indo-Pacific, spanning maritime security, supply chains, new technologies, and disaster response.

<><><> 

The 49th ASEAN Summit 2026 in Manila concluded with a series of important outcomes aimed at strengthening India’s engagement with Southeast Asia and the wider Indo-Pacific region. A report:

“The outcomes from the ASEAN summit reflected India’s growing regional engagement and reinforced ASEAN’s central role in India’s Act East Policy and its vision of a free, open, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

At the ASEAN-India Summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed series of initiatives covering maritime security, cyber forensics, space, nuclear energy, critical minerals, youth exchanges and education. PM also announced free e-visas for ASEAN tourists and enhanced scholarships at Nalanda University.

Likewise at the East Asia Summit, the PM proposed initiatives on seafarers’ safety, cybercrime cooperation, maritime heritage and academic exchanges. Three important regional documents were adopted on disaster management, online scams and regional stability.

On the bilateral front, PM Modi held meetings with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and the Prime Ministers of Singapore and Thailand to expand cooperation in key sectors. Ishfaq Shah, Manila Philippines.”

Uttar Pradesh’s draft electoral roll for the 2027 Assembly elections has been published. It comprises 13.58 crore voters after a net addition of 18.84 lakh electorates during the Special Summary Revision. UP Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said, the draft roll updates the previous final list released on April 10, 2026, after the Special Intensive Revision. More from our correspondent;

“Out of a total of 13.58 voters, Men account for 7.38 crore, while Women account for 6.20 crore, reflecting an addition of nearly 11 lakh female electors since the April 2026 roll. The roll includes 4,042 third-gender electors. Citizens in the 18-19 age group represent 11.83 lakh of the total voters. The revision is being conducted with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligible citizens turning 18. Eligible residents can file their claims and objections from November 17 to December 16, 2026. Citizens can use Form 6 for new voter inclusion, Form 7 for deletion of names, and Form 8 for correcting existing entries. Election officials will resolve all submitted claims and objections by December 28, 2026. The final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027. Voters can inspect the roll at all 1,73,730 polling booths across the state’s 403 Assembly constituencies, or check their status online via the CEO Uttar Pradesh Portal. SUSHIL TIWARI, AKASHVANI NEWS , LUCKNOW.”

Northern Railway has successfully facilitated the travel of nearly 1.82 crore passengers during the Puja and festive season this year. It registered an increase of around 10 lakh passengers compared to the corresponding period last year. Through strategic capacity enhancement, an expanded fleet of special trains, coach augmentations, and continuous demand monitoring, the zone significantly outperformed its previous year’s operational benchmarks. A report:

“According to the Northern Railway, seven thousand 85 special train trips were operated during the festive season of Diwali and Chhath Puja, compared to four thousand 666 trips last year. This means around 54 additional special train trips were operated every day to manage the festive rush. Daily passenger handling also increased from approximately 3 lakh 91 thousand to 4 lakh 14 thousand, accommodating nearly 22 thousand 700 additional passengers every day. Of the total passengers carried, around 1 crore 66 lakh travelled through regular train services, while 12 lakh 83 thousand were accommodated through special Trains on Demand services. This is Dilnashi Arzoo, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

<><><> 

Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw  reviewed  the measures  to ensure passenger convenience and safety during the return journeys following the Chhath festival. Mr Vaishnaw, monitored live CCTV feeds from various railway stations to assess crowd levels and identify locations experiencing high passenger pressure. He directed officials to take  measures to ensure smooth operation of trains and the safety of passengers in view of the heavy crowd. He also reviewed the holding areas established for passengers at major stations, including Patna, Danapur, Rajendra Nagar Terminal, Saharsa, Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga, and Jaynagar.

Cyclonic Storm Akvan formed over Bay of Bengal is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that cyclone Akvan will intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by this morning and further intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow evening. The cyclone is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on Friday. It is likely to bring winds of 120 to 130 kilometers per hour, gusting up to 145 kilometers per hour. The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh today. Heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy falls, is likely on Thursday and Friday. A report:

“The cyclonic storm AKVAN is moving west-northwest and is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam by Friday afternoon. The Amaravati Meteorological Centre has forecast heavy rainfall in coastal districts tomorrow and the day after.

Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the cyclone preparedness with senior officials. He directed them to take all advance measures to protect people from the cyclone’s impact. He also asked officials to continuously monitor the storm and keep relief and rehabilitation arrangements ready.

The government machinery has been put on alert. Collectors and Superintendents of Police in coastal districts have been directed to take precautionary measures in advance.

Officials have been directed to help farmers move crops ready for harvesting to safer places. They have also been directed to take all necessary steps to prevent disruption of power supply in areas likely to be affected by the cyclone. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

Telangana is also expected to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on Friday and Saturday.

Meanwhile, the Odisha government has identified over two lakh people across eight districts for possible evacuation. Disaster response teams have been deployed, and cyclone shelters are being prepared.

9th Naturopathy Day is being observed today across the country. The national-level programme will be organised at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy in Nagamangala, Karnataka. Organised by the Ministry of Ayush, the theme for this year is ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’. This year’s observance will place special emphasis on obesity prevention and addressing lifestyle-related disorders through healthy habits and preventive healthcare. The theme highlights the importance of balanced dietary practices, regular physical activity, yoga, stress management and naturopathic approaches in promoting overall health and well-being.

The United States has carried out precision strikes on an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missile launch site on Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. A US military official said, the strikes were carried out in response to Iran’s earlier attack on a US military base in Bahrain. US official said, the operation was conducted in self-defence against what Washington described as Iranian aggression targeting US soldiers and military assets. US aircraft used precision munitions to target the IRGC missile launch site. Iran’s military has warned ships against using what it described as fake American routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has also claimed to have shot down two US drones over the waterway.

A Russian military transport aircraft has crashed in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board. The An-12 aircraft came down in an uninhabited area near the village of Yagunovo in the Kemerovo region, around 3,000 kilometres east of Moscow. Russian Defence Ministry said a preliminary assessment points to a technical malfunction as the cause of crash. Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk said emergency teams quickly extinguished the fire at the crash site.

On to sports,

In Football, India clinched a record-extending 10th SAFF Championship title beating arch-rivals Pakistan 2-1 in a thrilling final to retain their crown at the National Stadium in Dhaka last night. The Blue Tigers also made history by winning the tournament for the third consecutive time. For India, Suhail Ahmad Bhat in 60th and Sandip Mandi in 88th minute scored the goals. India had booked their place in the final after defeating Bhutan 2-1 in the semi-final on Saturday. Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya has congratulated the Indian men’s football team for winning a historic hat-trick of SAFF Championship titles in Dhaka.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila, Philippines, today. The two summits are being hosted by the Philippines under its ASEAN Chairmanship for 2026. More from our correspondent:

During the summits, The Prime Minister is scheduled to engage with ASEAN leaders on strengthening India’s Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with the regional grouping and expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

At the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, leaders will review progress in implementing the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the ASEAN-India Plan of Action 2026-2030, and discuss the future direction of cooperation.

The Prime Minister will also attend the 21st East Asia Summit, which provides a platform for discussions on regional and global developments. The discussions are expected to focus on peace, stability, security and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region. Ishfaq Shah, Akashvani News Manila Philippines.

NITI Aayog will today launch a series of five National Workshops to draw lessons from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s twenty-five years as Head of Government. The workshops will focus on five themes: Leadership as Mission, Governance as Delivery, Development as Inclusion, Civilisational Identity and India’s Global Role. The series will continue until October next year. The first workshop, titled ‘Leadership as Mission’, will be held today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. It will feature first-hand accounts of key governance initiatives, including the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake, India’s response to COVID-19, the Lakhpati Didi initiative and the opening up of the space sector.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed twenty-five years as Head of Government on the 7th of October this year. He first assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat on the 7th of October 2001 and served in the post for more than twelve years.

The draft electoral rolls for all 403 Assembly constituencies across the 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh will be published today, as part of the Special Summary Revision-2027.

Chief Electoral Officer of state, Navdeep Rinwa, said that on the occasion of the publication of the draft electoral rolls, all District Election Officers will organise meetings with representatives of recognised national and state political parties at the district level. Copies of the draft electoral rolls will be provided to the representatives, and detailed information about the Special Summary Revision-2027 process will also be shared. The draft rolls will additionally be made available on the official websites of the respective District Election Officers for the information and convenience of the general public.

India has been re-elected to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council for the 2027-2030 term, during the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, Qatar. The 48-member ITU Council acts as the organization’s governing body between quadrennial Plenipotentiary Conferences. It overseas global telecommunication policies, strategic and financial plans, and working groups.

Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said, our resounding victory in the ITU Council elections reflects the trust and confidence the global community reposes in India’s growing capabilities and its commitment to shaping the future of telecommunications and digital connectivity.

Department of Telecommunications reaffirmed India’s commitment to building a connected, inclusive, secure and sustainable digital future for all.

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that Cyclone Akvan is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni around Friday noon as a very severe cyclonic storm. Talking  to Akashvani News, IMD Director General Mrityunjay Mohapatra said that the storm will reach a maximum wind speed of 120-130 kilometers per hour gusting up to 145 kilometers per hour. DG IMD said that the storm could cause extensive damage in coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh, including damage to thatched and tin houses, uprooting of trees and damage to electricity and telephone poles. He noted that the maximum impact is expected from Thursday night to Friday afternoon. Dr Mohapatra emphasized that all warnings are being issued to fishermen and fishing officials to completely suspend fishing activities in view of the severity of the approaching cyclone.

The Char Dham Yatra for this year has concluded with the closure of Badrinath Dham’s portals for the winter season with full rituals, Vedic chanting and religious traditions. With portals of Gangotri, Yamunotri, and Kedarnath were shut earlier, all four Himalayan shrines in Uttarakhand are now closed for the winter season.  Over 65 lakh pilgrims visited the four shrines this year, setting a new record. More from our correspondent:-

On the auspicious occasion of the temple’s closure, Badripuri echoed with chants of praise for Lord Badri Vishal. The temple was decorated with flowers, and the religious ceremonies were performed to the melodious tunes of an Army band. More than ten thousand devotees visited the shrine on the final day of the pilgrimage season.
As part of the traditional closing ceremony, temple Rawal Amarnath Namboodiri, dressed in the traditional attire of a Sakhi, ceremonially escorted Goddess Lakshmi into the sanctum sanctorum of Lord Badri Vishal. Thereafter, the movable idols of Lord Uddhav and Lord Kuber were brought out of the sanctum. Finally, the Nirvana idol of Lord Badri Vishal was covered with a ghee-soaked woollen blanket, and the temple portals were closed for the winter season at 9:37 PM.
During this pilgrimage season, more than 23 lakh 49 thousand devotees visited Badrinath Dham. Thus, even after the conclusion of the Char Dham Yatra, the winter pilgrimage season will continue in Uttarakhand. Anil Dutt Sharma, Akashvani News, Dehradun.

The inaugural season of the “AIR Rising Stars”, a nationwide series of special musical concerts exclusively by the young artists below 30 years of age, will be launched by Akashvani today. The first season of the concert series will be organised at 26 locations across the country from today to 30th of this month. These concerts will provide distinguished national platform to young and emerging musical artists to showcase their talent and connect with wider audiences. The initiative is being undertaken as part of the celebrations marking 90 years of Akashvani, reflecting its continued commitment to identifying, nurturing and promoting musical talent across generations. AIR Rising Stars seeks to carry this legacy forward by placing the spotlight on the next generation of performers. The concerts will be organised by 26 participating Akashvani Stations including  Shimla, Dehradun, Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi, Jaipur,  Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Imphal, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Puducherry, Jammu and  Guwahati. To encourage young artists and promote wider digital engagement, cash prizes and certificates will be awarded to the three participating artists whose performances secure the highest number of views on YouTube by 15th January next year The first  prize carries a cash amount of  20 thousand rupees, second prize will be of 15 thousand and the third will of 10 thousand rupees.

The world-famous Pushkar Fair formally begins today in Rajasthan with a traditional flag-hoisting ceremony and religious rituals. The fair, organised in three phases as a religious, cultural and cattle fair, will continue until November 24. During the week-long celebrations, religious ceremonies and cultural programmes will be held along the ghats of the sacred Pushkar Lake. Devotees, saints and tourists from across the country are arriving in Pushkar to participate in the festivities and take a holy dip in the sacred lake.

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, has called for moving the global just transition agenda from dialogue and exchange of experiences towards practical, country-driven implementation. Addressing the Fourth Annual High-Level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition under the UAE Just Transition Work Programme at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye) yesterday, the Minister reiterated India’s commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind. Noting that there can be no one-size-fits-all approach, he cited India’s sub-national heat action and disaster management plans, which address vulnerabilities of workers and communities, as well as the country’s renewable energy expansion that seeks to combine low-carbon development with affordable energy access. These examples underline the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning, he added. The Minister underlined the need for clearly defined and complementary roles for the UAE Just Transition Work Programme and the proposed Just Transition Mechanism.

At least four oil tankers have been damaged in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours, with the Iranian Navy reporting that a fourth tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine. UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has separately reported an attack on another tanker off the coast of Oman. According to the Iranian Navy, the tanker caught fire after colliding with a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. The Navy alleged that the vessel was navigating through a restricted maritime zone with its navigation systems switched off. The Iranian Navy also issued a warning to shipping operators, cautioning vessels against entering restricted maritime areas without coordination with the country’s armed forces. Separately, the UKMTO reported that a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz had been attacked seven nautical miles off Khasab in Oman. The incident comes amid heightened maritime security concerns in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route for global oil transportation.

The US Embassy in Madrid has issued a security advisory for American citizens travelling across Europe ahead of the holiday season, urging them to remain vigilant at crowded public places, including holiday festivals, tourist locations, transportation hubs, shopping malls and places of worship. The Embassy cautioned that large gatherings and public events could present potential targets for terrorist groups and criminals. The Embassy has urged US citizens to exercise extra vigilance while attending holiday festivals and events, particularly at locations with large crowds.

In Football, defending champions India will take on Pakistan in the final of the SAFF Championship in Dhaka, Bangladesh, today. India will be aiming to secure their 10th overall SAFF Championship title and make history by winning the tournament for the third consecutive time. The Blue Tigers booked their place in the final after defeating Bhutan 2-1 in the semi-final on Saturday. Pakistan, meanwhile, will be making their first-ever appearance in a SAFF Championship final. The two sides have met 30 times in senior internationals, with India winning 17 matches, Pakistan four and nine ending in draws. Today’s clash will, however, be their first meeting in a senior SAFF Championship final.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will undertake a two-day visit to Philippines beginning today. During the visit, he will participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, which is being hosted tomorrow by the Philippines as the ASEAN Chair for 2026.

 

India-ASEAN relations are a central pillar of India’s Act East Policy and our vision for the Indo-Pacific. The visit comes as India and ASEAN are celebrating 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, and will commemorate 35 years of Dialogue Relations and five years of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2027. The ASEAN-India Summit will review progress in the implementation of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the ASEAN-India Plan of Action 2026-2030, and chart the future direction of cooperation.

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India’s relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India’s Act East Policy and occupies a central place in the vision of MAHASAGAR. In his departure statement, Mr Modi said that India’s ties with ASEAN, rooted in centuries of civilizational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations.

 

The Prime Minister emphasized that he is looking forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. He added that he is also looking forward to give further momentum to the shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity.

 

<><><> 

 

Indian Ambassador to ASEAN Srinivas Gotru said India’s engagement with ASEAN has gained significant momentum under India’s Act East Policy, with growing cooperation in trade, investment and defence. Speaking to Akashvani News, Mr Gotru said the annual India-ASEAN Summit remained one of the most significant events in India’s diplomatic calendar, providing an opportunity for leaders to review relations and set new directions for cooperation. He added that India-ASEAN trade has grown nearly 25 times in three decades.

Government’s health expenditure has more than tripled to 4.14 lakh crore rupees in 2023-24 from 1.30 lakh crore rupees in 2013-14. This was stated in the National Health Accounts 2023-24 report released by the Union Health Ministry. As per the report, government spending rose to increase its overall share of total health spending by 14.9 percentage points, while per capita public healthcare expenditure nearly tripled from 1,042 to 2,959 rupees. Direct out-of-pocket expenditure by families dropped significantly by 21.5 percentage points.

 

Social security health spending nearly doubled from 6 percent to 11 percent, and private health insurance jumped from 3.4 percent to 10.2 percent.

Today is the National Press Day. It reaffirms the vital role of a free, responsible, and ethical press in strengthening the Nation’s democracy. The day marks the establishment of the Press Council of India, PCI which began its operation on this day in 1966. Established as an independent body, the PCI’s primary role is to ensure that the press maintains high standards of journalism while remaining free from external influences. This year the theme of the National Press Day Celebration is “Journalism: Populist or Responsible. We have a report from our correspondent:

 

“National Press Day serves as an important reminder of the vital role that the press plays in shaping the country’s democracy. Since its establishment, the Press Council of India has worked tirelessly to uphold press freedom,maintain journalistic standards, and address challenges facing the media. From tackling issues like media ethics and press safety to adapting to the digital age, the Council continues to guide and support the media in its mission to inform, educate, and empower the public. National Press Day not only celebrates the achievements of the press but also reinforces the responsibility it carries in building a more informed and transparent society, ensuring that the future of journalism remains strong, free, and responsible. Anand Kumar for Akashvani News, Delhi.”

The four-day long Chhath Puja concluded this morning with Usha Arghya, the morning prayer offered to the Rising Sun. On the final day today, devotees gathered early in the morning to offer prayers and water to the rising Sun. After completing the rituals, devotees broke their 36-hour fast by having the prasad. We have a report  from our Patna correspondent:

 

“Aadideva Namastubhyam Praseeda Mama Bhaskara, Divakara Namastubhyam Prabhakara Namostute.”

“The four-day Chhath Mahaparv, symbolising devotion to the Sun God, gratitude towards nature and social harmony, concluded across Bihar with religious fervour and enthusiasm. On the fourth and final day of the festival, devotees offered Usha Arghya to the rising Sun this morning. In Patna, the state capital, and various other districts, a large number of devotees gathered at Chhath ghats since early morning. With the first rays of the Sun, devotees standing in water offered the second Arghya to the Sun God and prayed for the prosperity and good health of their families. Following the final rituals of the four-day festival, devotees performed Paran, thereby concluding their 36-hour-long fast without food and water. Savita Pareek, Akashvani News, Patna.“

 

In Jharkhand, Chhath ghats across the state were filled with devotees even before the first rays of the morning Sun. More from correspondent:

 

“In the state capital, Ranchi, Chhath devotees stood in waist-deep water at Kanke Dam, Bada Talab, Hataniya Talab and other water bodies to worship the Sun God and pray for happiness and prosperity. As the first rays of the Sun appeared in the eastern sky, the atmosphere reverberated with chants of ‘Jai Chhathi Maiya’. Similar scenes of devotion were witnessed at various Chhath ghats across the state, including the banks of the Swarnarekha River in Jamshedpur, Pampu Talab in Dhanbad and Shivganga in Deoghar, as well as in Bokaro. Devotees offered Arghya to the Sun God with milk and water and subsequently performed Paran, breaking their 36-hour-long fast without food and water. The festival concluded peacefully in a devotional atmosphere, with elaborate security arrangements in place. Mahvish Rahman, Akashvani News, Ranchi.”

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has proposed reforms to simplify the rules for governing cab rental businesses, promote ease of doing business and strengthen passenger safety. Under the proposed reforms, operators will be allowed to offer cabs with or without drivers. The minimum fleet requirement will be reduced from 50 to five vehicles, with at least 2 cabs per place of operation. The requirement for branches in five tourist cities is removed. The four-day long Chhath Puja will begin today with the ‘Nahay-Khay’ ritual in different parts of the country. Dedicated to Surya Dev or the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, the festival is observed with strict purity, fasting, and rituals along riverbanks and ghats. The Nahay-Khay’ is marked by ritual bathing and preparation of food while observing strict cleanliness and purity. Traditionally, devotees prepare Kaddubhaat as prasad, marking the beginning of the four-day festival.

 

The second day will be observed as ‘Kharna’. Devotees will observe a day-long fast and break it in the evening after offering prayers and consuming prasad. This will be followed by the rigorous ‘nirjala’ fast.
On the third day, devotees will gather at rivers, ponds and other Chhath ghats in the evening to worship Chhathi Maiya and offer ‘arghya’ to the setting sun.

The festival will conclude on Monday morning with devotees offering ‘arghya’ to the rising sun.

Throughout the year, Akashvani broadcasts and organizes a series of special programmes across the country based on the Gandhian Philosophy. Public Service Broadcasting Day inspires Broadcasters to carry forward the ideals and teachings of Mahatma Gandhi, to every corner of the country.
